prompt.context: Your client is the CFO of Aperture Laboratories, a leading US biopharmaceutical company with a market cap greater than $150B. Aperture develops and manufactures a diversified range of products and in particular prides itself on saving millions of human lives every year. The company is under investor pressure because of its slow firm value growth over the next 10 years. Investors are very anxious to see significant changes announced at the firm in the next quarter.
prompt.question: The CFO has already identified and evaluated a number of high-growth, promising, but capital-intensive projects, and she does not have enough cash to invest in any of the opportunities. What does she need to do next?

clarifying_info.q: Are there any tax implications from a potential asset sale?
clarifying_info.a: The deal has been structured by JP Morgan to be tax-free.

clarifying_info.q: Does the NPV figure for each project include the capital investment?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the NPV figures are net of the capital investment required.

exhibits.title: Aperture Business Segments
exhibits.shows: A bubble chart plotting Aperture's business units by 5-year revenue CAGR (y-axis) and degree of specialization required (x-axis, increasing rightward). Bubble size represents sales volume. Business units shown are: Oncology drugs, Primary care pharmaceuticals, Emerging market drugs, Consumer health, Animal health, Nutrition, Specialty care pharmaceuticals, and Established products.

exhibits.title: Investment Opportunities
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot showing six potential investment projects, each plotted by NPV ($B) on the y-axis and Capital Investment Required ($B) on the x-axis.

projects.name: Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants
Research new formulations for existing product portfolio

framework: Raise capital: identify the fastest and most impactful ways to generate cash (divestiture of a non-core business unit, issuing new equity, raising debt, canceling existing projects to free budget)
Evaluate each capital-raising option on speed, size of proceeds, strategic fit, and feasibility (e.g., availability of buyers, leverage capacity, investor optics)
Select divestiture of the most separable, lowest-strategic-fit business unit as the primary lever
Deploy capital: use raised proceeds to invest in highest-NPV, capital-constrained project portfolio (profitability-index ranking)
Address investor communication: ensure the announced changes are visible and significant enough to satisfy investors within the quarter
Mitigate risks: identify risks for each action (deal execution, timing, project failure) and outline mitigation steps

questions.prompt: Which business unit should Aperture divest, and why?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify Animal Health as the best divestiture candidate on three grounds: (1) it has one of the lowest 5-yr CAGRs among all segments; (2) it is strategically misaligned with Aperture's core mission of saving human lives; (3) its low specialization requirements mean a larger pool of potential acquirers, making the sale more feasible and faster. Candidates should walk through the exhibit and articulate their reasoning rather than being prompted.

questions.prompt: How much capital can Aperture raise from divesting Animal Health?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply Animal Health sales by the EV/Sales multiple provided. Answer is $14.7B. If asked about taxes, the deal is structured to be tax-free.

math.setup: Animal Health sales ($4.2B) x EV/Sales multiple (3.5x) = proceeds

questions.prompt: Given a capital budget of $14.7B from the divestiture, which projects should Aperture invest in to maximize NPV?
questions.guidance: Excellent candidates will compute a profitability index (NPV / Capital Investment) for each project, rank them, and then select projects in descending order until the budget is exhausted. The optimal selection is: (1) Build R&D center in China (PI=1.67, capex $6B), (2) Research new formulations for existing portfolio (PI=1.67, capex $3B), (3) Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing (PI=1.40, capex $5B). Total capex = $14B, total NPV = $22B, leaving $700M undeployed. A very strong candidate will also suggest a use for the remaining $700M (e.g., share buyback or dividend).

math.setup: Profitability Index = NPV / Capital Investment for each project; rank descending; accumulate capex until budget ($14.7B) is exhausted
steps: Research new formulations for existing portfolio: $5B / $3B = 1.67

Ranked order (highest PI first): China R&D (1.67, $6B), New formulations (1.67, $3B), US manufacturing cost-cut (1.40, $5B), License respiratory (1.25, $4B), GLP-1 agonist (1.11, $9B), Sales force (1.00, $3B)
Select top projects within $14.7B budget: China R&D ($6B) + New formulations ($3B) + US manufacturing ($5B) = $14B total capex
math.answer: Invest in: Build R&D center in China ($6B, NPV $10B), Research new formulations ($3B, NPV $5B), Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing ($5B, NPV $7B). Total capex $14B, total NPV $22B. Remaining $0.7B can be returned to shareholders via buyback or dividend.

recommendation: Aperture should divest its Animal Health division, which is strategically non-core (no human-life mission alignment), has low growth (among the lowest CAGRs in the portfolio), and has a broad buyer pool due to low specialization requirements
The divestiture, structured tax-free through JP Morgan, is expected to generate approximately $14.7B (Animal Health sales of $4.2B x 3.5x EV/Sales)

Deploy $14B of the proceeds into the three highest profitability-index projects: Build R&D center in China ($6B, NPV $10B), Research new formulations for existing products ($3B, NPV $5B), and Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants ($5B, NPV $7B), generating a combined NPV of $22B
Return the remaining ~$700M to shareholders via a buyback or special dividend to further address investor pressure
risks: Inability to find a qualified buyer for the Animal Health division at the expected 3.5x multiple
Timing risk: deal completion may extend beyond the quarter in which investors expect significant changes to be announced
Execution risk: new capital projects may take longer than expected or fail to deliver projected NPV
Market/regulatory risk: GLP-1 agonist or R&D center projects face competitive or regulatory headwinds
next_steps: Engage JP Morgan to formally launch the Animal Health sale process and establish a target close timeline
Secure CFO and board sign-off on the three selected capital deployment projects
Prepare investor communication materials announcing the divestiture and growth investment plan for the next quarter
Develop mitigation plans for each identified risk (e.g., line up backup buyers, set project milestone gates)
